h1: SEO in Patna without the link spam that gets you penalised
metaTitle: SEO Company in Patna: Coaching, Hospitals, Hindi
metaDescription: Cheap Patna packages still sell bulk directory links that get sites penalised. We audit first, then do the slow version, on a 90-day baseline guarantee.
answer: Plenty of cheap Patna SEO packages still run on bulk directory submissions and private blog networks. That worked in 2014. Today it earns a manual action or a link-spam demotion, and the recovery takes longer than the campaign did. SEO in Patna worth paying for starts by auditing the links you already have.
takeaways: Before anything else: open Search Console, check **Manual actions**, and export your link report. If you inherited a spam profile, nothing else you do will work.
The worst possible time to get demoted in Patna is result week or admission season. That's when a coaching institute earns most of its year.
Hindi voice search is genuinely large here, and it phrases questions differently from typed search. Most Patna sites answer neither.
Your site is being opened on a ₹9,000 Android on a congested tower. That's the device your Core Web Vitals are actually scored on.

sections.h2: What a ₹6,000-a-month package can physically contain
body: Start with arithmetic rather than accusation. SEO needs four disciplines — technical, content, links, reporting. At Patna market rates, a monthly fee in the single-digit thousands buys somewhere between four and eight hours of one generalist's time, total, across all four.

Nobody can audit, write, earn a link and report in eight hours a month. So the package has to be automated to exist at all, and the only parts of SEO that automate cheaply are the parts Google explicitly treats as spam: bulk directory submissions, article-spinner blog posts, comment and profile links, and placements on private blog networks sold by the hundred.

This isn't a Patna problem in origin — the same packages sell in every tier-2 city in India. It's a Patna problem in concentration, because the local market is price-led and the buyers are often first-time SEO clients who have no way to tell a real link from a rented one.

callout.title: Ask one question before you renew
callout.body: "Send me the list of every domain that linked to us last month." A real answer arrives in a spreadsheet with fifteen or twenty domains you can visit and recognise. A bad answer arrives as a screenshot of a rankings tool, or as a list of 400 sites you have never heard of.

sections.h2: What a demotion actually costs, in admission-season terms
body: Google has two separate ways of dealing with a spam link profile, and it's worth knowing which one you're facing.

A **manual action** is a human reviewer at Google applying a penalty to your site. It appears in Search Console under Manual actions, it's explicit, and it needs a documented reconsideration request to lift. An **algorithmic demotion** — the kind that arrives with a spam update — shows you nothing at all. No message, no notice, just traffic that halves over a fortnight and stays halved until the next update recalculates.

Now put that on Bihar's calendar. Board results, entrance results and counselling windows compress a coaching institute's enquiry volume into a handful of weeks. A demotion in an ordinary month is expensive. A demotion in result week removes the season. And because reconsideration and recovery run on Google's schedule rather than yours, you cannot buy your way back in time — the fastest honest route back is usually a quarter, and often longer.

sections.h2: Auditing an inherited link profile before you touch anything
body: If you've had an agency before, this is where we start — before content, before a single technical fix. There's no point building on a foundation that's about to be penalised.
The sequence is boring and it's the most valuable month of the engagement.
numbered: **Check Manual actions in Search Console.** Ten seconds. It settles which of the two problems you have.
**Export every linking domain** from Search Console, and cross-check with a third-party index because Search Console's list is not complete.

**Classify by hand.** Real editorial link, legitimate directory, irrelevant directory, obvious network. The last category is usually recognisable within seconds — same template, same footer, hundreds of unrelated outbound links.

**Try removal first where it's feasible**, then disavow the rest. Google's own guidance is that most sites never need a disavow file — it's for cases where you have a manual action or genuinely expect one. Uploading one casually can cost you links that were helping.
**Stop the tap.** If the old agency is still building, the cleanup is pointless. Cancel before you clean.
**Then start real work.** Earned links from Bihar press, education and health publications, institutional pages and genuine partnerships. Slower, fewer, permanent.

sections.h2: Coaching institutes: the calendar is the strategy
body: Patna's coaching economy is one of the densest in India — the clusters around Boring Road and Musallahpur Hat exist because demand for BPSC, SSC, railway, NEET and JEE preparation is year-round and enormous.

Search demand for it is not year-round. It arrives in cliffs: a result declaration, a notification, a counselling window, an admission deadline. Enquiries in those weeks can outweigh whole quiet months, and the pages that catch them have to have been ranking beforehand.

That produces a specific content plan. Result and notification pages, published before the date and updated the hour it lands. Cut-off and previous-year-paper pages that rank all year and spike on the day. Batch, fee and faculty pages that answer what a parent actually asks.

One uncomfortable note on results pages: publishing selected students' names and marks is standard practice locally, and it does draw enormous traffic. Get written consent, and don't publish a claim you can't substantiate. This is a category where a competitor complaint has real consequences, and where fabricated results damage more than rankings. The [SEO for coaching institutes](/seo-for/coaching-institutes) page goes into the structure in detail.

sections.h2: Hospitals and diagnostics: the query is Hindi, the site is English
body: Patna's health search runs through a small set of very large public institutions — AIIMS Patna, IGIMS, PMCH — plus a dense private layer along Bailey Road and around Kankarbagh. Patients and, more often, their attendants search under pressure and they search in Hindi.

They also increasingly speak the query rather than type it. Voice search in Hindi is phrased as a full sentence — a spoken question about which doctor treats a condition, or where a particular scan is available and what it costs — where typed search is two or three words. A site written only in clipped English service names matches neither.

What ranks is unfashionable: a page per department, a page per doctor with real credentials and registration details, a page per major test or procedure with an honest price range, and clear appointment information. That's also what Google's quality guidance expects from health content. Nothing about it is clever — most Patna hospital sites simply haven't done it.

There's a hard rule here too: don't publish outcome guarantees or comparative superiority claims for medical services. It's a regulatory risk in India, and it's the kind of content that ages badly the moment anyone checks it.

sections.h2: Devanagari that reads like a person wrote it
body: The default approach to Hindi content is to run the English site through a translation tool and publish. It doesn't work, for two separate reasons.

The first is human. Machine-translated Hindi is instantly recognisable to a Hindi reader — the register is wrong, the sentence order is English, and honorifics land oddly. People leave. The second is that Google's spam policies treat automatically translated text published without human review as low-quality content, so you're spending money to build pages that are working against you.

The version that works is smaller: pick the ten or fifteen pages where a Hindi searcher actually converts, and have them written in Hindi by someone who speaks it, covering the same ground rather than the same sentences. Add transliterated variants, because a large share of Bihar's searchers type Hindi phonetically on an English keyboard — *patna me best coaching* is a real query pattern and it is not the same string as its Devanagari equivalent. We covered the wider question in [SEO in Hindi and Indian languages](/journal/seo-in-hindi-and-indian-languages).

sections.h2: The phone your site is actually being opened on
body: Bihar's internet is mobile-first to a degree that changes engineering decisions. The typical visitor is on an entry-level Android with limited memory, on a network that is fine at 6am and congested at 9pm.

This matters for rankings specifically, not just for user experience. Google's page experience signals draw on field data collected from real Chrome users — which means your scores come from those phones, on that network, not from the desktop where your developer ran a test and got a green score.

The fixes are ordinary and they're worth real budget here: compress images properly, cut third-party scripts (a chat widget, three analytics tags and a popup library is a common combination and it costs seconds), stop the layout shifting while it loads, and test on a genuinely cheap phone with the network throttled.

faqs.q: How do I know if my previous Patna SEO agency built spam links?
faqs.a: Open Search Console, check Manual actions, then export your linking domains. Visit twenty of them at random. If they're template blogs stuffed with unrelated outbound links, or directories in languages your customers don't read, you have a network profile. A real profile has domains you recognise and could explain.

faqs.q: How long does it take to recover from a link penalty?
faqs.a: For a manual action, weeks to months after the cleanup is genuinely complete and a reconsideration request is accepted. For an algorithmic demotion, until the next relevant update recalculates — and nobody can give you that date honestly. Either way, budget a quarter minimum and treat faster promises as sales talk.

faqs.q: What does SEO cost in Patna?
faqs.a: You'll find local packages advertised in the single-digit thousands per month, which cannot fund four disciplines and generally funds automated links instead. We charge from ₹75,000/month, or ₹40,000/month for smaller sites, ex-GST, month-to-month after the first quarter, and you keep every asset if you leave.

faqs.q: Do I need Hindi content to rank in Patna?
faqs.a: For consumer-facing categories — coaching, healthcare, retail, local services — yes, and transliterated Hindi typed on an English keyboard matters as much as Devanagari. Write it rather than translating it. Ten well-written Hindi pages will outperform a machine-translated mirror of your entire site, which Google treats as low-quality anyway.

faqs.q: Is it worth doing SEO for a coaching institute that already fills its batches?
faqs.a: Depends on what you're filling them with. If your enquiries come from referrals and hoardings, search is where you reach the students who don't know your name yet — particularly out-of-district and out-of-state ones. If you're already turning students away, spend on retention instead. We'd rather say that than take the retainer.
